sections.title: Start and choose a goal
paragraphs: Create your adventurer and choose Start Adventure. A new character begins on Tutorial Island. Returning progress resumes your character and tutorial state.
Progress comes from skill XP, higher levels, better equipment, supplies, and completed quests. Skills cap at level 99. Hitpoints starts at level 10; the other implemented skills start at level 1.

After the tutorial, a useful first goal is to prepare cooked food and a bronze kit, then explore the Starter Town area of Main Overworld. The linked journeys explain the gathering, smithing, fishing, and rune loops.

sections.title: Touch and desktop controls
paragraphs: The touch controls below are verified against the local mobile implementation recorded under Version and coverage. They are an unpublished draft awaiting the final published game source. Desktop mouse and keyboard bindings remain available.

On touch screens, Bag opens Inventory, Equipment, Combat, Skills, and Quests; Chat opens messages. Scroll within the drawer to reach its controls. Bag and Chat open one at a time; Close returns to the world.

Hold a target or item for half a second, lift your finger, then tap a menu choice. Holding opens choices without also performing the primary action. Menus remain open until a choice, Cancel, or an outside tap.

Dragging the world rotates the camera without walking or using a target. Rotation, pointer cancellation, or backgrounding cancels pending gestures. Keep game text fields unfocused when using desktop camera keys; arrow keys move the camera, while character movement uses selected destinations.

rows.action: Walk or perform a default world action
rows.touch: Tap the ground, object, or NPC. Combat follows the existing targeting and tick rules.
rows.desktop: Left-click a ground destination, object, or NPC.

rows.touch: Hold a world target or item for half a second; lift, then tap Talk-to, Attack, Use, Examine, or another available choice.
rows.desktop: Right-click to open the context menu, then click a choice.

rows.touch: Open Bag and tap an item for its current primary action. Hold for applicable choices such as Use, Equip, Eat, or Drop.
rows.desktop: Left-click an item for its preferred primary action; right-click for its choices.

rows.touch: Hold an inventory item, choose Use, then tap the second item or world target. Recipe ingredients, tools, and skill requirements still apply.
rows.desktop: Choose Use on an inventory item, then click its target.

rows.touch: Open Bag's Equipment or Combat tab. Tap equipped gear to unequip it; use Combat to select a melee training style or toggle Auto Retaliate.
rows.desktop: Open Equipment or Combat and click the corresponding gear or setting.

rows.touch: Drag the world with one finger.
rows.desktop: Hold the middle mouse button and drag, or use the arrow keys.
Scroll the mouse wheel over the game view.

rows.touch: Tap a destination to walk; pinch to change the minimap zoom.
rows.desktop: Left-click a destination to walk; use the wheel to change zoom.

rows.touch: Open the map button, drag to pan, pinch to zoom, and close with X.
rows.desktop: Open the map button; wheel zooms and left-drag pans. Escape closes it.

rows.touch: Open Chat, type a message, and tap Send or use the keyboard's Enter key.
rows.desktop: Enter focuses chat and submits a message; Escape leaves the field.

rows.touch: With the service open, hold an inventory, bank, or shop item and tap the transfer quantity. X opens an amount prompt; Cancel dismisses it.
rows.desktop: Right-click the item and choose a quantity. X opens the same amount prompt.

rows.touch: Tap Stop to cancel walking, the combat target, queued interaction, selected Use item, or a repeated skill session. Hitpoints, progress, and cooldowns are preserved.
rows.desktop: The touch toolbar provides Stop; normal mouse and keyboard bindings remain available.

rows.touch: Home saves completed character progress and returns to the fixed Arcade address. If saving fails, stay in the game and retry Home after the message.
rows.desktop: Exit to Arcade is also available in character creation and recovery screens.

rows.touch: Use Close, X, or Cancel as shown. Tap outside an action menu to dismiss it.
rows.desktop: Use close buttons. Escape closes NPC dialogue, the bank, world map, and touch drawers.

sections.title: Finish Tutorial Island
paragraphs: Talk to each instructor before practising, and return to report the result. The guidance marker points to your next instructor or activity. Talking alone does not finish a practical lesson; gates follow your tutorial step.

Follow this order: Tutorial Guide, Woodcutting, Fishing, Firemaking and Cooking, Mining and Smithing, melee Combat, Ranged, Magic, Runecrafting, Crafting, then the Bank Tutor. The guide sends you to Main Overworld after banking is complete.

At the forge, mine copper and tin for three bronze bars: two make the sword blade and one makes arrowheads. Assemble the blade with the strapped wooden handle. Keep the arrowheads for the ranged lesson.

For magic, equip the plain staff and keep ember runes in your inventory; attacking a chicken from range uses a rune automatically. For crafting, soften clay at the pond, stand near the bench, and use soft clay on the borrowed ring in your inventory.

The bank lesson requires depositing the supplied coin at one booth and withdrawing it at the other, then reporting to the Bank Tutor. Both booths share your bank. If supplies are missing, talk to the current instructor again for the lesson's recovery items.

sections.title: Gather, make, trade, and bank
paragraphs: Carry the matching tool, click a resource or choose its gathering action, and wait for attempts. Your skill level, tool, resource, and available inventory space affect what you can do. The inventory has 28 slots; stackable items share a slot.

Mining feeds Smithing and Crafting. Woodcutting feeds Firemaking and Fletching. Fishing and animal drops feed Cooking. Firemaking creates temporary fires for cooking; cooked food heals, while raw and burnt items are different outcomes.

Use a furnace to smelt and an anvil to forge. Some outputs are components that need a separate inventory assembly step. Recipe tables show required levels, ingredients, tools, stations, and XP; owning a component does not automatically make the finished tool.

Runecrafting begins with ember runes at level 1, then water at 10, earth at 20, and air at 30. Combination recipes start at 40 and require the combination unlock as well as essence and a secondary rune. Pouches hold extra essence subject to their level and capacity rules.

Talk-to explains NPC roles and quest gates. Trade and shop options handle merchant stock; a value in an item table alone does not guarantee a merchant currently sells it. Use bank booths to store items in the shared bank and free inventory space.

Bank menus offer Deposit or Withdraw quantities of 1, 5, 10, All, or X. Shops offer Buy or Sell quantities of 1, 5, 10, 50, or X. Choose X to enter an amount, or Cancel to leave the prompt. Available stock, coins, and storage space still constrain transfers. The mobile draft exposes these existing choices through hold menus, with inventory and service panels visible together.

sections.title: Combat and survival
paragraphs: Choose Attack on an enemy. Combat locks a target and runs on attack cooldowns, range, hit rolls, and equipment requirements. Walking away changes your position and engagement; it does not guarantee that a chasing enemy immediately gives up.

Melee supports Attack, Strength, and Defense training styles. Bows use compatible arrows, and staffs use compatible runes. Ranged ammunition can be equipped or selected from inventory; magic runes come from inventory. The current runtime spends one ammunition item on each consuming attack, including misses.

Damage above zero grants four XP per damage point to the attack's training skill and one XP per damage point to Hitpoints. Melee uses the selected training style; ranged and magic award their respective skill XP.

Eat cooked food from your inventory to restore Hitpoints, up to your maximum. Food has its own eating delay, and you cannot eat on the same tick as attacking or casting. Check each food's healing amount before relying on it.

At zero Hitpoints, you return to the current world's default safety spawn with full health and cleared combat state. The reviewed defeat handler retains inventory and equipment. Enemy drops appear as ground loot; choose Take to collect them. Enemy pages show their current drop tables, aggression, and respawn data.

sections.title: Quest objectives and unlocks
paragraphs: Six quests are defined in the reviewed runtime. Talk to their NPCs to begin or check progress, then follow the dialogue to finish. Turn-in quests consume the requested materials; the quest log records objectives and status.

Tanner Rusk's quest is one early option. Boars and wolves are stronger than tutorial chickens, so bring suitable equipment and food before collecting his materials. Advanced merchant quests open their associated trade access.

rows.quest: Hides of the Frontier — Tanner Rusk
rows.objective: Turn in 4 boar tusks and 2 wolf fangs.
rows.reward: 200 coins, 125 Crafting XP, tannery merchant access.

rows.quest: Proof of the Deepforge — Thrain Deepforge
rows.objective: Turn in 6 coal, 2 gold ore, and 1 uncut emerald.
rows.reward: 200 Smithing XP and advanced ore stock.

rows.quest: Proof of the Yew — Advanced Fletcher
rows.objective: Turn in 1 yew handle, 1 yew longbow, and 1 yew shortbow.
rows.reward: 250 Fletching XP and the full buyer ledger.

rows.quest: Proof of the Grain — Advanced Woodsman
rows.objective: Turn in 1 willow log, 1 maple log, and 1 yew log.
rows.reward: 200 Woodcutting XP and full merchant stock.

rows.quest: From Net to Harpoon — Fishing Teacher
rows.objective: Turn in 1 each of raw shrimp, trout, salmon, tuna, and swordfish.

rows.quest: Moulds of the Trade — Elira Gemhand
rows.objective: Use her borrowed jewelry to imprint clay moulds, fire them, and hold a ring, amulet, and tiara mould.
rows.reward: 150 Crafting XP and all three mould unlocks. Borrowed jewelry is removed on completion.

sections.title: Settings, saves, and limits
paragraphs: Use the Run button to toggle running. Combat controls let you choose a melee training style and toggle Auto Retaliate. Inventory context menus can set a preferred primary action for a click or tap; that preference is saved.

Progress saves to local browser storage every 10 seconds and through lifecycle save hooks. It includes your character, position, skill XP, inventory, bank, equipment, quests, unlocks, run mode, and item preferences. The current storage key is osrsClone.progress.v2. A different browser or device has separate local storage; there is no account-based cloud-save workflow in this revision.
Keep browser site data to retain progress. Starting a fresh session or clearing the game's storage resets local progress. This wiki update does not modify the game's saves.

In the mobile draft, Home saves completed character progress before returning to Arcade. If saving fails, the game stays open with a retry message. Backgrounding stops active player actions and saves completed progress. Rotation or pointer cancellation cancels pending gestures. Character creation has touch appearance choices, a draggable preview, a scrollable form, and Exit to Arcade; WebGL recovery offers Reload and Exit without erasing stored progress.

Inventory and bank drag reordering retain their existing desktop implementation. Touch item actions and bank transfers use tap and hold choices; touch drag reordering is not implemented by this mobile change.

Mobile-owner testing used Chromium touch emulation. Physical phones and tablets, Safari, a real soft keyboard, and operating-system gesture interruptions were not tested. The wiki checks its own rendering and links; it does not establish those game-device results.

Combat, ranged, magic, tutorial lessons, and quests are implemented even though the export only creates nine gathering and production skill pages. A spellbook progression system and the old standalone North Road Camp region are not documented as playable features. The touch controls above remain a local draft until the final published game revision is reviewed and pinned.
